## Licensed Data Collection

## Faculty Research Data Collection

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Who can deposit data in the Faculty Research Data Collection?

UC Berkeley senate faculty, or a researcher designated by the faculty member to use their allocation, may deposit data for publication.

Funding for this data publishing service, which is a component of the Data Storage Allocation pilot program, was made available following advocacy by the Senate Committee on Information Technology (CIT) and DIVCO to address data storage issues faced specifically by faculty. As a result, the scope of this initial pilot is focused on senate faculty. 
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Why should I deposit data in the Faculty Research Data Collection?

* To comply with funder or publisher data sharing requirements  
* Ensure reliable, managed access to data  
* Increase scholarly impact through discoverability  
* Collaborate with research teams  
* Select a CC0 or CC BY license
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I have data that updates regularly, can I deposit it with the Faculty Research Data Collection?

The Faculty Research Data Collection is not designed to support continuously updated data, as all datasets must go through a manual curation and review process. Please reach out to [librarydataservices@berkeley.edu](mailto:librarydataservices@berkeley.edu) if you would like to discuss depositing snapshots of dynamic data.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### What data protection levels are safe to deposit with the Faculty Research Data Collection?

Data up to protection level 2 may be deposited with the Faculty Research Data Collection. 

For guidance on data classification, review the Information Security Office’s [How to Classify Research Data resource](https://security.berkeley.edu/how-classify-research-data) or contact the [Research Data Management Program](https://researchdata.berkeley.edu/home).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I need to publish code \- where can I do that?

The UC Berkeley Library Data Services program recommends the Zenodo repository for publishing code. Please contact [librarydataservices@berkeley.edu](mailto:librarydataservices@berkeley.edu) with questions. 
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### I want to publish my data in a different repository. What are my options?

The UC Berkeley Library provides memberships to a variety of repositories, including Dryad and ICPSR. Please contact [librarydataservices@berkeley.edu](mailto:librarydataservices@berkeley.edu) for guidance.
:::
